mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.4% quarter-over-quarter signals improved household demand, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or IC drops below 0.05 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals labor market tightness that raises wage pressure and inflation expectations, which in turn erodes corporate margins and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -0.5% month-over-month signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or IC drops below 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% per annum signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below -1.0% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or IC drops below 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month signals labor market strength that raises wage pressure and inflation expectations, which erodes margins and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year window.
